name: Lovell proportionality (ρ)
title: Do two dealers swap share, or just ride the market?
what: A correlation-like measure that is valid on shares, and now a market-partial version whose false-alarm rate we checked.
pick_line: Math + Engineering, as Jared chose: the increment-partial ρ holds its size; the 11-12 level version does not.
data: Public FR Y-9C proxy (E4: 4 dealers, 62 quarters) and simulations; descriptive only
one: Remove the market from increments, not levels: then partial ρ keeps its 5% false-alarm rate.

left.sub: false alarms at a 5% test when two dealers only share the market

right.sub: same simulation, T = 62; power 99% on a real swap

findings.h: On shares, the usual correlation calls every market co-move a relationship.
findings.t: Simulated pairs that move together only through the market: raw ρ on clr levels rejects 100% of the time at T = 40 and T = 62. Removing the market from levels (the 11-12 prototype) still gives 12.7–13.3%.

chart.title: False-alarm rate at a 5% test (market-only pairs, T = 62)

findings.note: The raw ρ bar is cut at 30%; its value is 100%. Pass band set in advance: 2–8% at both T = 40 and T = 62.

findings.h: The increment version still finds a real swap.
findings.t: With an independent swap planted between the two parts, the increment partial ρ detects it 99.0% of the time at T = 62 and 89.7% at T = 40 (bar: 80% at T = 62).

findings.h: Honest limit: a noisy market proxy breaks every version.
findings.t: If the market factor is only measured with noise (sd half its own), false alarms jump to 98.8–100% for all three procedures at both lengths. Partial ρ is only as good as the market control.

chart.title: False-alarm rate with a noisy market proxy (T = 62)

findings.h: Engineering: a small library reproduces 11-12 exactly and is fast.
findings.t: E4 JPM–GS ρ −0.6976291 and level-partial −0.8820532 reproduced (error ≤ 4e-16). All 124,750 pairs for 500 parts × 62 quarters in 0.03 s. On the increment version, JPM–GS is −0.788 (exact cyclic-shift p = 0.018).
findings.note: Bars show the size of a negative ρ (all three are negative). The −0.788 p-value is for this one pair, not adjusted across pairs.

findings.h: Build 2026-11-23: size holds from T = 30, but only with an exact market proxy.
findings.t: Pre-registered rerun, 1,000 runs per cell: false-alarm rate 5.5% (T = 40) and 7.0% (T = 62), power 98.8% at T = 62. T = 30 is the shortest panel that passes. A market proxy with even 0.10 sd of noise pushes false alarms to 49–87%.

chart.title: False-alarm rate of increment-partial ρ, T = 62 (bar ≤ 8%)
